title: Fix directory crash in plan check and re-enable job planning
summary: Git::show_file returns None for a non-blob path, so no caller can crash on a directory. Athena's plan checks turn a planned directory or non-plain-relative path into a major finding that sends the plan back. Then job_plan is re-enabled and the crash and job 20261017-204355-358k go in the changelog. Audience: the Athena maintainer running athena go.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and integration tests; cargo test --locked, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check pass.
Fix show_file itself so no caller can crash on a directory, and also harden the plan check.
Criteria run tests that exercise a directory path and a docs/ plan.
Enforced by tests and the plan check, not by prose.
The changelog entry and doc comments are written for an outside reader.
The behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier runs.
One focused change across the git crate, the plan check, config and changelog.
All changes are Rust and TOML.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause is in Git::show_file, which uses cat-file -e (true for trees) and then cat-file blob. The fix checks the object type, for example with cat-file -t or by resolving to a blob, and returns None for non-blobs.

The plan_findings function in crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs, or the exists closure passed to plan_record in run.rs, is where the directory and bad-path checks go. The path shape check must not need the filesystem.

A directory has no blob, so after the show_file fix exists=false. For Modify or Delete that already gives a major finding, but 'docs/' with Create would slip through. So an explicit path-shape and is-directory check is needed, and the directory check can use the git tree.
The fake-agent test harness in crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs can script a planner output with a directory path.
athena.toml is a governance file, and the request names it explicitly, so it is a listed deliverable.

acceptance_criteria.text: A git test in crates/athena-git shows that show_file on a directory path (for example a tree such as 'docs/' or 'docs') returns Ok(None) with no error, and that it still returns the bytes for a real file. Run: cargo test -p athena-git.

A test with a fake planner whose plan lists 'docs/' shows that Athena emits a major finding for that path, that the job moves on to the next plan round, and that nothing crashes or returns an error. Run: cargo test.
Plan checks give a major finding, not an error, for any planned path that is a directory, is absolute, contains '..', is empty, or ends in '/'. A unit test covers each case. Run: cargo test.
cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check all pass, as does xtask's boundary test.
athena.toml has [job_plan] enabled = true, and no other setting in that file changes.
CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] names the job-planning crash on a directory path and job 20261017-204355-358k.

Outcome check: replaying the failing input, a plan that lists docs/, no longer produces the 'git cat-file blob <base>:docs/ failed' error. This is shown by the new tests failing on the old code and passing on the new.

out_of_scope: Changing the planner prompt or the critic stage
Changing planner or critic budgets in athena.toml
Fixing the other callers of show_file individually
Pre-existing-check handling from job 20261017-204355-358k's own request
departures: Slightly higher acceptance than the reference because the request is detailed and gives a numbered plan. Cost and time are a bit higher because the change touches three crates and needs a full workspace test, clippy and xtask run.
